summary: Evald Lidén worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his fil.kand. at Uppsala University (1883–1895). He was a PD at Uppsala in 1895, then served as acting professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit (1899) and Head (1917–1929) at Gothenburg.

Philosopher Evan Thompson studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto (1990), also studying under Francisco Varela. His posts include York University, Toronto (~2005–2013), and the University of British Columbia (2013).

Evelyn Frederick Charles Ludowyk worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Richmond College and served as Professor of English at the University of Ceylon from circa 1942 to 1956.

Philosopher Evert Willem Beth studied at Utrecht University (~1925–1935). He held academic posts at the University of Amsterdam from 1946 to 1964 and at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1952 to 1953.

Evgenij Mihajlovič Medvedev was an Indologist and historian who studied at Moscow State University (~1951–1956). He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1956–1957) and later as Director at Moscow State University (1960).

Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his BA and studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1998–2009), where he was appointed Chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion in 2009.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello, Parimal G. Patil, and Michael Puett, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian specialist who studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Uhlenbeck, Caland, van Wijk, and Vogel. He taught at Carpentier Alting Stichting Lyceum before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1939–1972).
F. Garritsen was a scholar in Indology. He completed his studies at Utrecht University under the instruction of Jan Gonda.

F. Gelpke was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar who studied at Rostock and Göttingen under Wackernagel, Oldenberg, and Emil Sieg, completing his Dr. phil. by 1929. In 1932, he served as an assistant at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin.

F. J. Richards, who worked in Indology, history, and archaeology, studied at Exeter College (1893–1902; B.A. 1897, M.A. 1902). He founded The Mythic Society in 1909 and served as Honorary Lecturer on Indian Archæology at SOAS in 1934.

F. M. G. Lorimer worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology after studying at Somerville College (1902–1905). Lorimer held posts at the Bodleian Library, Royal Asiatic Society (1932–1940), and Royal Horticultural Society.
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.
Fa Yao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. Fa Yao was attested in 2026 as a Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago.

Fabian Wilhelm af Ekenstam worked in Indology and religious studies. He earned his fil.dr. at Lund University (1805–1808), where he served as Docent (1809) and Adjunkt (1812) of Theology before teaching philosophy at Katedralskolan, Linköping (1822–1837).

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will (~1994–1999). Circa 2001, she became Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Venice, Naples, and Tokyo, being taught by Massimo Raveri and Adriana Boscaro. He held posts at Sapporo University and later UC Santa Barbara (~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" from 1969 to 2004. She held academic posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1994–1998) and the University of Florence (~1998).

Fabrizio Ferrari works in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and SOAS, where he worked as a teaching assistant (2005–2008), later serving as professor at Chester (2008–2018) and Padua (from 2018).
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a post as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.
